options.misconception: Correct application of the principle
Reported joules instead of converting to kilojoules
Used a factor of one hundred rather than one thousand
Divided mass by latent heat instead of multiplying

questions.explanation: During a phase change the temperature stays constant while energy goes into rearranging the structure, so Q equals mass times specific latent heat. Here 168 g times 524 J per g gives 88032 J, or 88.03 kJ after dividing by one thousand.
questions.hint: Q = m L, then convert joules to kilojoules.

Dropped the number of moles from the calculation
Left the answer in joules instead of kilojoules

questions.explanation: When heat capacity is given per mole, the heat required is Q equals n times Cm times delta T. Multiplying 0.7 mol by 49 J per mol K by 18 K and dividing by one thousand yields 0.62 kJ.

questions.stem: Trial 711503799: an ideal gas of carbon dioxide with 3.3 mol expands isothermally at 308 K from 2.3 L to 9.2 L; how much heat must be supplied, in kJ?

options.misconception: Halved the temperature in the nRT factor
Correct application of the principle
Altered the volume ratio by adding one to it
Omitted the logarithm from the work expression

questions.explanation: For an ideal gas at constant temperature the internal energy does not change, so by the first law the heat supplied equals the work done by the gas, nRT ln(Vf over Vi). With the given volumes and temperature this is 11.71 kJ; heat must flow in to balance the expansion work.
questions.hint: At constant T for an ideal gas, Q = W = nRT ln(Vf/Vi).

questions.stem: Trial 550804874: starting at 425 K, an ideal gas of xenon with gamma 1.4 expands adiabatically from 1.7 L to 5.4 L; find the final temperature.

options.misconception: Inverted the initial-to-final volume ratio
Correct application of the principle
Used gamma rather than gamma minus one as the exponent
Assumed temperature scales linearly with volume

questions.explanation: For a reversible adiabatic ideal-gas process T V raised to gamma minus one is constant, so Tf equals Ti times (Vi over Vf) to the power gamma minus one. With gamma 1.4 the exponent is 0.4, giving a final temperature of 266.9 K; expansion cools the gas because it does work with no heat entering.
questions.hint: Use Tf = Ti (Vi/Vf)^(gamma - 1) for adiabatic expansion.

Divided pressure by the volume change
Doubled the volume change before multiplying

questions.explanation: At constant pressure the work done by the gas is P delta V. With pressure 113 kPa and volume increase 2.8 L, and using one kPa litre equal to one joule, the work is 316 J. A rigid constant-volume step would instead do zero work, but this process has a moving piston.

questions.explanation: Because the device returns to its starting state each cycle, the change in internal energy over a full cycle is zero, so the net work output equals the net heat input Qh minus Qc. That gives 630 J per cycle; the rejected heat is not available as work.
